column2: Theobald Boehm (design); Boehm and Mendler flutes measured by D. C. Miller; riser of a Pearl PF-661 measured by UNSW
Boehm cylinder-bore flute with parabolic head-joint, normal scale of Boehm 1871 as recomputed by Miller 1922, B foot-joint
Boehm flute, 13 large holes, 3 small holes (D# and D trill, small C#), silver tube, B foot
none: a published scale assembled from several instruments, not one accessible specimen
unstated by Boehm and Miller; the scale is for A=435 and is rescaled to A=440 by Boehm's published Schema rule (derived rows are labelled)

hybrid published description, not any recorded flute: hole positions, bore, taper, cork and mouth-hole are Boehm and Mendler data from Miller 1922, the riser is the measured Pearl PF-661 riser from UNSW; the maker and model of the University of Iowa flute are unstated (u-uiowa-model-identity)
hole-01 is nearest the cork (D# trill hole) and hole-16 is farthest (C4 hole of a B foot); positions are measured from the cork face along the bore axis
435 as published; 440 declared here as the design pitch for the derived axial-position-a440-schema rows (a design choice of the instrument, never read from a recording)
